bibl.title: Sensory inputs control the integration of neurogliaform interneurons into cortical circuits

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how Reelin-expressing neurogliaform interneurons acquire their pattern of afferent connectivity during the first postnatal week
span.quote: Here we report that, during early development, superficially positioned Reelin-expressing neurogliaform interneurons in the mouse somatosensory cortex receive afferent innervation from both cortical and thalamic excitatory sources.

span.label: what regulates the balance between thalamic and intracortical inputs onto developing superficial interneurons
span.quote: However, the mechanisms by which the formation of these complex cortical circuits is regulated, including the establishment and maintenance of an appropriate balance between thalamic and intracortical inputs, are unknown.

span.label: shows superficial Reelin interneurons receive direct thalamic input during development, and that NMDA receptor signalling through it sets the ratio of thalamic to intracortical connectivity
span.quote: These results suggest that thalamic inputs are critical in determining the balance between local and long-range connectivity and are fundamental to the proper integration of Reelin-expressing interneurons into nascent cortical circuits.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These results suggest that thalamic inputs are critical in determining the balance between local and long-range connectivity and are fundamental to the proper integration of Reelin-expressing interneurons into nascent cortical circuits.

span.label: cortical interneuron circuit integration
span.quote: Despite the central role of these interneurons in cortical function, the developmental steps that regulate the establishment of their specific connectivity patterns are not understood.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: To confirm the absence of cortically evoked synaptic responses, we performed in vitro electrophysiology and at the same time filled layer I Re + interneurons with biocytin to reveal their morphology.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Developing interneurons discriminate between otherwise similar glutamatergic afferents according to which postsynaptic receptor subtype those afferents engage
span.quote: Re + interneurons distinguished between seemingly similar inputs on the basis of the postsynaptic receptors that the afferents impinge on.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: NR2B-containing NMDA receptors are preferentially allocated to the dendritic postsynaptic sites that receive thalamic input, giving ascending afferents a privileged signalling channel
span.quote: Our results extend these observations and suggest that there is a preferential allocation of NR2B-containing NMDARs to the postsynaptic sites in the dendrites of Re + interneurons that receive thalamic input.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: NMDA receptor activation drives the interneuron's integration into the nascent circuit, so that losing it both stunts the arbor and shifts the balance of afferents toward local cortical sources
span.quote: Together these data suggest that activation of NMDARs mediates the proper integration of maturing interneurons in the brain.

span.label: sparse electroporation plus focal rabies injection yields one starter cell per brain, so the traced inputs belong to a single identified interneuron
span.quote: The focal rabies injection together with the sparse electroporation of ventrally generated interneurons further diluted by their dispersion during tangential migration to the cortex 15 allowed us to target one starter cell in each experimental brain

span.label: anatomical tracing is confirmed functionally by optogenetic mapping with TTX and 4AP, isolating monosynaptic responses
span.quote: In accordance with the anatomical tracing, we recorded light-evoked monosynaptic excitatory responses from these neurons in the presence of tetrodotoxin (TTX) to block polysynaptic events and 4-aminopyridine (4AP) to enhance presynaptic vesicular release

span.label: the requirement is timed: removing the receptor at P3 reproduces the defect and at P6 does not, placing the critical window between them
span.quote: After electroporating Dlx5/6-Cre ER (estrogen receptor) and CAG-STOP-GFP plasmids in NR1 fl/fl mice at E15.5, we subsequently administered tamoxifen at P3 or P6 and analyzed Re + interneuron morphology at P8. Tamoxifen administration at P3 but not at P6 phenocopied the morphological defects observed in the embryonic Dlx5/6-Cre ablation experiments ( Supplementary Fig. 13 ). These results indicate that NR2B-containing NMDARs driven by the thalamic inputs are required in Re + interneurons between P3 and P6 for their proper morphological development.

span.label: the effect is subunit-specific - NR2B-containing receptors are required, NR2A-containing ones are not
span.quote: In exploring the mechanisms underlying this observation, we found that thalamocortical synapses use NMDA receptors (NMDARs) containing the NR2B subunit and that cell-autonomous removal of these receptors (but not NR2A-containing receptors) led to severe morphological defects in Re + interneurons.

span.label: AMPA receptor signalling remains intact and is not sufficient: the cells still fail to develop axons or integrate
span.quote: Remarkably, even in the presence of substantial glutamatergic signaling through AMPARs, Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons failed to develop proper axonal processes and to integrate properly into nascent cortical circuits.

span.label: the total input count is preserved while its composition flips, so this is reallocation rather than loss
span.quote: Furthermore, the total number of presynaptic traced cells was not significantly different between control (190 ± 55) and Dlx5/6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl (150 ± 47; P = 0.646) interneurons ( Fig. 7d ).

span.label: The authors could not rule out that some cortical glutamatergic signalling survived their viral tetanus-toxin blockade of intracortical input.
span.note: what this limits: the completeness of the silencing: WE COULD NOT FORMALLY EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY THAT RESIDUAL CORTICAL GLUTAMATERGIC SIGNALING TO Re+ INTERNEURONS PERSISTED
span.quote: Although we observed a marked decrease in VAMP2 levels upon injection with the AAV-flex-TeLC.eGFP virus ( Fig. 3e ), we could not formally exclude the possibility that residual cortical glutamatergic signaling to Re + interneurons persisted.

span.label: The complete-intracortical-blockade genotype yielded very few animals, so a second mouse line had to be generated to enlarge the sample.
span.note: what this limits: the complete-blockade analysis: IN AN EFFORT TO INCREASE THE SAMPLE SIZE FOR THIS ANALYSIS, WE GENERATED MICE containing a second allele combination, because the first genotype was too rare
span.quote: In an effort to increase the sample size for this analysis, we generated mice containing a Bhlhb5 Cre allele and loxP -flanked ( fl ) Munc18 ( Stxbp1 ) alleles 24 .

span.label: the absence of neuromodulatory input is overridden by inference from the authors' own prior work, which says it must appear eventually
span.note: what this limits: the claim that these cells lack neuromodulatory input: WE DID NOT OBSERVE APPRECIABLE INPUTS ... FROM ASCENDING NEUROMODULATORY FIBERS, supported by SUPPLEMENTARY FIG. 3 AND DATA NOT SHOWN
span.quote: Notably, unlike in other interneuron populations we have investigated, such as VIP- and SST-expressing interneurons ( Supplementary Fig. 3 and data not shown), we did not observe appreciable inputs onto the Re + interneurons from ascending neuromodulatory fibers such as those from the dorsal raphe and the nucleus basalis (although, on the basis of our previous findings 16 , we infer such innervation must ultimately be established).

span.label: interneuron-to-interneuron connectivity did not change significantly, with only three mutant animals
span.note: what this limits: the interneuron-to-interneuron connectivity comparison: NOT SIGNIFICANTLY CHANGED (CTRL: 27% +/- 6 VERSUS 42% +/- 4, P = 0.103) - a null on a small sample rather than an established absence
span.quote: In contrast, interneuron afferent connectivity was not significantly changed in Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons (Ctrl: 27% ± 6 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 42% ± 4, P = 0.103) ( Fig. 7f ).

span.label: the cross-species claim about the proportion of these interneurons is explicitly a speculation
span.note: what this limits: the cross-species reading: THE INCREASE IN ABUNDANCE OF THIS POPULATION ACROSS SPECIES IS SPECULATED TO REFLECT THE LARGER DEMAND FOR ASSOCIATIVE FUNCTIONS IN THE HUMAN BRAIN
span.quote: The increase in abundance of this population across species is speculated to reflect the larger demand for associative functions in the human brain

span.label: whether VIP interneurons use intrinsic programs or unidentified activity sources is left open
span.note: what this limits: the generality of the activity-dependence claim: VIP+ INTERNEURONS MAY USE EITHER INTRINSIC GENETIC PROGRAMS OR AS-YET-UNIDENTIFIED SOURCES OF ACTIVITY
span.quote: These results indicate that Re + neurogliaform interneurons are critically reliant on electrical activity to mature and integrate into cortical circuits, whereas VIP + interneurons may use either intrinsic genetic programs or as-yet-unidentified sources of activity.

span.label: monosynaptic rabies tracing, adapted to single starter cells and to developmental time points
span.quote: In addition to providing specific insights regarding the development of connectivity onto Re + interneurons, our findings suggest that monosynaptic tracing using the rabies virus provides an effective method for determining the afferent connectivity of cortical neurons at different developmental time points.

span.label: the finding that specific rather than global activity refines connectivity, used as the frame for this result
span.quote: These observations emphasize that understanding how brain wiring is achieved will require a case-by-case examination of how different cell types and the cortical microcircuits they contribute to are assembled.

span.label: the same rabies-tracing experiment repeated in a LARGER AND DIFFERENT SUBSET of superficial interneurons, including VIP- and calretinin-expressing subtypes
span.note: eliminates: a bias in the method itself - if rabies tracing simply fails to label some synapse types, the absence of nucleus basalis input onto Re+ interneurons would be an artefact of the tracer rather than a fact about the circuit · outcome: held
span.quote: Furthermore, to rule out a bias of the rabies tracing to GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses, we carried out the same experiment in a larger subset of superficial interneurons, including VIP- and calretinin-expressing subtypes.

span.label: balance here is a RATIO of afferent sources whose total is conserved - thalamic falls from 60% to 16% while intracortical rises from 14% to 42%, with the same number of presynaptic cells
span.quote: Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons showed a severe reduction in thalamic afferent connectivity (Ctrl: 60% ± 6 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 16% ± 2, P < 0.01) and a concomitant increase in intracortical pyramidal cell innervation (Ctrl: 14% ± 1 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 42% ± 2, P < 0.0001) ( Fig. 7c,e,f ).

span.label: the same glutamatergic input is distinguished not by its transmitter but by which postsynaptic receptor it acts on, which is what lets one afferent source matter and another not
span.quote: In exploring the mechanisms underlying this observation, we found that thalamocortical synapses use NMDA receptors (NMDARs) containing the NR2B subunit and that cell-autonomous removal of these receptors (but not NR2A-containing receptors) led to severe morphological defects in Re + interneurons.

span.label: Re-positive and VIP-positive interneurons are used throughout as a built-in contrast: every manipulation that impairs one leaves the other intact
span.quote: Re + but not VIP + interneurons failed to migrate to appropriate laminae and displayed impaired morphological maturation after an overall dampening of neuronal excitability. Similarly, Re + but not VIP + interneurons failed to develop normal axonal arbors and dendritic trees after sensory deprivation, genetic blockade of thalamic glutamate release or blockade of NMDAR-dependent currents.

span.label: the absence of cholinergic input is scoped to this age, not to this cell type - the authors expect it to appear later
span.quote: Notably, unlike in other interneuron populations we have investigated, such as VIP- and SST-expressing interneurons ( Supplementary Fig. 3 and data not shown), we did not observe appreciable inputs onto the Re + interneurons from ascending neuromodulatory fibers such as those from the dorsal raphe and the nucleus basalis (although, on the basis of our previous findings 16 , we infer such innervation must ultimately be established).

span.label: claim_type: mechanism
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: mechanism — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Attenuation of ascending sensory, but not intracortical, excitation leads to axo-dendritic morphological defects in these interneurons. Moreover, abrogation of the NMDA receptors through which the thalamic inputs signal results in a similar phenotype, as well as in the selective loss of thalamic and a concomitant increase in intracortical connectivity.

span.label: method: monosynaptic rabies tracing from single starter interneurons, ChR2-assisted circuit mapping, whisker deprivation, and cell-autonomous conditional removal of NMDA receptor subunits
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: electrophysiology — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: The focal rabies injection together with the sparse electroporation of ventrally generated interneurons further diluted by their dispersion during tangential migration to the cortex 15 allowed us to target one starter cell in each experimental brain

span.label: phenomenon: activity-dependent assembly of cortical microcircuits
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: cortical interneuron circuit integration — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: These observations emphasize that understanding how brain wiring is achieved will require a case-by-case examination of how different cell types and the cortical microcircuits they contribute to are assembled.

span.label: extends → previous work showing that sensory experience shapes the topography of the sensory cortices (refs 33-37)
span.quote: Our findings extend previous work demonstrating that sensory experience shapes the topography of the sensory cortices 33 – 37 directly and not through second order cortical neurons.

span.label: builds-on → the authors' own preceding study of how dampened excitation affects interneuron positioning and maturation (ref 9)
span.quote: In an effort to understand the contribution of activity to interneuron development, we compared in a preceding study how dampening excitation of interneurons at particular developmental time points affected the positioning and maturation of specific interneuron subtypes 9 .

span.label: contradicts → the classical view that layer IV is the primary recipient of ascending thalamic sensory input
span.quote: Although layer IV has been classically regarded as the primary recipient of ascending sensory information carried via thalamic terminals 11 , we found, unexpectedly, that during the first postnatal week, in addition to inputs from intracortical sources, Re + interneurons in layers I–III also receive direct thalamic inputs.

span.label: extends → the authors' own earlier finding that Re-positive but not VIP-positive interneurons require activity to mature
span.quote: We observed marked differences in the requirement for activity in VIP multipolar cells, which were apparently unaffected by attenuated levels of excitation, unlike Re + neurogliaform cells, whose migration and morphological development were markedly impaired

span.label: supports → retinogeniculate work showing that specific activity, not overall activity level, drives afferent refinement
span.quote: These observations emphasize that understanding how brain wiring is achieved will require a case-by-case examination of how different cell types and the cortical microcircuits they contribute to are assembled.

span.label: supports → published rabies tracing of mature VIP interneurons showing no bias toward thalamic synapses
span.quote: These results are in agreement with recently published data on rabies tracing of mature VIP + interneurons 32 . VIP + interneurons present in the visual cortex receive substantial innervation from intracortical populations and the nucleus basalis, with a minor contribution from the dLGN, indicating that the rabies virus does not preferentially label thalamic synapses over cortical or cholinergic ones.

span.label: thalamic —causes→ neurogliaform
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — SCOPE: attenuating ascending sensory but NOT intracortical excitation produces the defect - the sign of the claim depends on which afferent is cut
span.quote: Attenuation of ascending sensory, but not intracortical, excitation leads to axo-dendritic morphological defects in these interneurons. Moreover, abrogation of the NMDA receptors through which the thalamic inputs signal results in a similar phenotype, as well as in the selective loss of thalamic and a concomitant increase in intracortical connectivity.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · NMDA —causes→ thalamic
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named the genotype rather than the receptor. This sentence names both and states the causal chain: abrogating the NMDA receptors 'through which the thalamic inputs signal' results in the selective loss of thalamic connectivity. — strength of the relation: 0.9 — removing the receptor cuts thalamic input from 60% to 16% while intracortical rises 14% to 42%, with total input unchanged - reallocation, not loss
span.quote: Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons showed a severe reduction in thalamic afferent connectivity (Ctrl: 60% ± 6 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 16% ± 2, P < 0.01) and a concomitant increase in intracortical pyramidal cell innervation (Ctrl: 14% ± 1 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 42% ± 2, P < 0.0001) ( Fig. 7c,e,f ).

span.label: NR2B —distinct-from→ NR2A
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHICH SUBUNIT'S REMOVAL PRODUCES THE DEFECT. 'thalamocortical synapses use NMDA receptors (NMDARs) containing the NR2B subunit and ... CELL-AUTONOMOUS REMOVAL OF THESE RECEPTORS (BUT NOT NR2A-CONTAINING RECEPTORS) LED TO SEVERE MORPHOLOGICAL DEFECTS in Re+ intern[eurons].' Both subunits are present; only one is load-bearing for the morphology, and the contrast is a loss-of-function result rather than a difference in expression. Q-466. · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: In exploring the mechanisms underlying this observation, we found that thalamocortical synapses use NMDA receptors (NMDARs) containing the NR2B subunit and that cell-autonomous removal of these receptors (but not NR2A-containing receptors) led to severe morphological defects in Re + interneurons.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · AMPAR —distinct-from→ NMDA
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named only AMPARs. This sentence sets the two against each other in the paper's own construction - 'the contribution of NMDARs VERSUS AMPARs'. — strength of the relation: 0.95 — AMPAR signalling is present and explicitly insufficient, which is what makes the requirement receptor-specific rather than activity-general
span.quote: Remarkably, even in the presence of substantial glutamatergic signaling through AMPARs, Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons failed to develop proper axonal processes and to integrate properly into nascent cortical circuits.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · neurogliaform —distinct-from→ VIP
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named only VIP. This sentence names both, says 'marked DIFFERENCES in the requirement for activity', and uses 'UNLIKE' between the two cell types. — strength of the relation: 1 — the built-in contrast: every manipulation impairing one leaves the other intact
span.quote: Re + but not VIP + interneurons failed to migrate to appropriate laminae and displayed impaired morphological maturation after an overall dampening of neuronal excitability. Similarly, Re + but not VIP + interneurons failed to develop normal axonal arbors and dendritic trees after sensory deprivation, genetic blockade of thalamic glutamate release or blockade of NMDAR-dependent currents.

span.label: neurogliaform —distinct-from→ VIP
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER DEVELOPMENT REQUIRES ACTIVITY. 'We observed marked differences in the requirement for activity in VIP MULTIPOLAR CELLS, WHICH WERE APPARENTLY UNAFFECTED BY ATTENUATED LEVELS OF EXCITATION, UNLIKE RE+ NEUROGLIAFORM CELLS, WHOSE MIGRATION AND MORPHOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT WERE MARKEDLY IMPAIRED.' Two interneuron classes in the same manipulation, and only one needs the activity - so a study using either alone would conclude the opposite about interneuron development in general. Q-486. · strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS De-Marco-Garc-a2015-sensory-inputs-control-the-integration-of-ne[4]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: We observed marked differences in the requirement for activity in VIP multipolar cells, which were apparently unaffected by attenuated levels of excitation, unlike Re + neurogliaform cells, whose migration and morphological development were markedly impaired 9 .

span.label: AMPAR —distinct-from→ NMDA
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — RE-GROUNDS De-Marco-Garc-a2015-sensory-inputs-control-the-integration-of-ne[3]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Abrogation of NMDAR activity leads to aberrant Re + interneuron differentiation To assess the contribution of NMDARs versus AMPARs to the development of Re + interneurons, we carried out genetic and pharmacological blockade of the different types of receptors.

span.label: NMDA —causes→ thalamic
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — RE-GROUNDS De-Marco-Garc-a2015-sensory-inputs-control-the-integration-of-ne[1]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Moreover, abrogation of the NMDA receptors through which the thalamic inputs signal results in a similar phenotype, as well as in the selective loss of thalamic and a concomitant increase in intracortical connectivity.

span.label: Mann-Whitney U test
span.quote: ( k ) Average EPSC amplitude at −70 mV in layer I interneurons after stimulating layer II in control TeLC and Emx1-TeLC mice (Ctrl = 14 cells; Emx1-TeLC n = 4 cells, P = 0.0008, Mann-Whitney test).

span.label: t-test
span.quote: ( d ) Quantification of the total number of presynaptic neurons per starter cell in control (Ctrl; n = 6) and Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl ( n = 3) mice (mean values ± s.e.m.; unpaired t -test; P = 0.646).

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: We found that each Re + interneuron received inputs from 196 ± 48 (s.e.m.) presynaptic neurons located in cortical and subcortical structures.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: ( f ) The proportion of thalamic (Thal), cortical excitatory (Ecx) and cortical interneuron (Icx) inputs to control ( n = 6 mice) and Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons ( n = 3 mice) (Thal, P = 0.002; Ecx, P = 3.8E-06; Icx, P = 0.103).

span.label: unpaired t-test on morphological measures
span.quote: After electroporating Dlx5/6-Cre ER (estrogen receptor) and CAG-STOP-GFP plasmids in NR1 fl/fl mice at E15.5, we subsequently administered tamoxifen at P3 or P6 and analyzed Re + interneuron morphology at P8. Tamoxifen administration at P3 but not at P6 phenocopied the morphological defects observed in the embryonic Dlx5/6-Cre ablation experiments ( Supplementary Fig. 13 ). These results indicate that NR2B-containing NMDARs driven by the thalamic inputs are required in Re + interneurons between P3 and P6 for their proper morphological development.

span.label: proportion of presynaptic partners by source
span.term: proportion of presynaptic partners by source
span.quote: Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons showed a severe reduction in thalamic afferent connectivity (Ctrl: 60% ± 6 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 16% ± 2, P < 0.01) and a concomitant increase in intracortical pyramidal cell innervation (Ctrl: 14% ± 1 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 42% ± 2, P < 0.0001) ( Fig. 7c,e,f ).

span.label: Contrary to the classical view that layer IV is the main recipient of ascending sensory input, Reelin-expressing interneurons in layers I-III receive direct thalamic afferents during the first postnatal week.
span.quote: Although layer IV has been classically regarded as the primary recipient of ascending sensory information carried via thalamic terminals 11 , we found, unexpectedly, that during the first postnatal week, in addition to inputs from intracortical sources, Re + interneurons in layers I–III also receive direct thalamic inputs.

span.label: Whisker deprivation left cortical layering and interneuron migration intact but severely truncated the axons and dendrites of Reelin-expressing interneurons.
span.quote: While this manipulation did not perturb cortical layering or interneuron migration ( Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 7a,b ), analysis of the morphological maturation of Re + interneurons revealed severely truncated axonal arbors and dendritic trees ( Fig. 2c,e–g and Supplementary Fig. 7c ).

span.label: Genetic silencing of thalamic transmission with tetanus toxin light chain reproduced the deprivation phenotype, establishing thalamic activity as necessary for axo-dendritic development.
span.quote: These results suggest that thalamic activity is fundamental to the axo-dendritic development of Re + interneurons and are consistent with our previous findings indicating that, in contrast to VIP + subtypes, Re + interneurons are affected by alterations in activity 9 .

span.label: Blocking intracortical glutamate release, by contrast, left the morphological development of the same interneurons unaffected.
span.quote: These results show that we can substantially reduce the afferent intracortical drive to Re + interneurons without noticeably impairing their development.

span.label: Thalamic afferents recruit a larger NR2B-containing NMDA receptor component than cortical afferents do, as measured by ifenprodil blockade.
span.quote: We found that light-evoked NMDAR-mediated synaptic responses showed a larger NR2B-component in VGlut2-ChR2 than in Emx1-ChR2 mice ( Fig. 4d–f ).

span.label: The maturation requirement is specific to NR2B: NR2A-null and AMPA-receptor-blocked interneurons developed normally.
span.quote: These defects were specific to the loss of NR2B-containing receptors, as Re + interneurons developed normally in NR2A −/− ( Grin2a −/− ) mice ( Fig. 6 ), as well as after blockade of AMPA receptors in vivo ( Supplementary Fig. 12 ).

span.label: The NMDA receptor requirement is confined to a narrow window between postnatal days 3 and 6.
span.quote: These results indicate that NR2B-containing NMDARs driven by the thalamic inputs are required in Re + interneurons between P3 and P6 for their proper morphological development.

span.label: Cell-autonomous NMDA receptor deletion rewired the afferent balance, cutting thalamic input roughly fourfold while tripling intracortical pyramidal input, with total input count unchanged.
span.quote: Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons showed a severe reduction in thalamic afferent connectivity (Ctrl: 60% ± 6 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 16% ± 2, P < 0.01) and a concomitant increase in intracortical pyramidal cell innervation (Ctrl: 14% ± 1 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 42% ± 2, P < 0.0001) ( Fig. 7c,e,f ).

span.label: superficial Reelin interneurons receive direct thalamic input in the first postnatal week, contrary to the layer IV expectation
span.quote: Although layer IV has been classically regarded as the primary recipient of ascending sensory information carried via thalamic terminals 11 , we found, unexpectedly, that during the first postnatal week, in addition to inputs from intracortical sources, Re + interneurons in layers I–III also receive direct thalamic inputs.

span.label: each interneuron received about 196 presynaptic partners, 56% of them thalamic
span.quote: We found that each Re + interneuron received inputs from 196 ± 48 (s.e.m.) presynaptic neurons located in cortical and subcortical structures. Surprisingly, a considerable proportion of these inputs originated in the ventroposteromedial (VPM) and posteromedial (POm) nuclei of the thalamus (VPM and POm: 56 o 6%). In addition, Re + interneurons received local afferents from pyramidal and subplate cells (14 ± 2%), as well as from other interneurons (30

span.label: no appreciable input from dorsal raphe or nucleus basalis was found at this age
span.quote: Notably, unlike in other interneuron populations we have investigated, such as VIP- and SST-expressing interneurons ( Supplementary Fig. 3 and data not shown), we did not observe appreciable inputs onto the Re + interneurons from ascending neuromodulatory fibers such as those from the dorsal raphe and the nucleus basalis (although, on the basis of our previous findings 16 , we infer such innervation must ultimately be established).

span.label: the same tracing method did find nucleus basalis input to VIP and calretinin interneurons, so the absence is not a method artifact
span.quote: Furthermore, to rule out a bias of the rabies tracing to GABAergic and glutamatergic synapses, we carried out the same experiment in a larger subset of superficial interneurons, including VIP- and calretinin-expressing subtypes. We found that, in contrast to Re + interneurons, these populations of superficial interneurons received innervation from the nucleus basalis at P6, indicating that the rabies tracing strategy does not preclude per se the tracing of these synapses

span.label: removing NMDA receptors cut thalamic input from 60% to 16% and raised intracortical from 14% to 42%
span.quote: Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons showed a severe reduction in thalamic afferent connectivity (Ctrl: 60% ± 6 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 16% ± 2, P < 0.01) and a concomitant increase in intracortical pyramidal cell innervation (Ctrl: 14% ± 1 versus Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl : 42% ± 2, P < 0.0001) ( Fig. 7c,e,f ).

span.label: the total number of presynaptic cells did not change
span.quote: Furthermore, the total number of presynaptic traced cells was not significantly different between control (190 ± 55) and Dlx5/6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl (150 ± 47; P = 0.646) interneurons ( Fig. 7d ).

span.label: the requirement falls between P3 and P6
span.quote: After electroporating Dlx5/6-Cre ER (estrogen receptor) and CAG-STOP-GFP plasmids in NR1 fl/fl mice at E15.5, we subsequently administered tamoxifen at P3 or P6 and analyzed Re + interneuron morphology at P8. Tamoxifen administration at P3 but not at P6 phenocopied the morphological defects observed in the embryonic Dlx5/6-Cre ablation experiments ( Supplementary Fig. 13 ). These results indicate that NR2B-containing NMDARs driven by the thalamic inputs are required in Re + interneurons between P3 and P6 for their proper morphological development.

span.label: cortical layering and pyramidal cell distribution were normal despite the interneuron defects
span.quote: Indeed, the total number and the distribution of pyramidal cells in superficial and deep layers were similar in control and sensory-deprived brains ( Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 7a,b ). Similar results were obtained after genetic blockade of thalamic transmission ( Fig. 2b–g and Supplementary Fig. 8 ). In spite of the normal layering of the cortex at P8, these manipulations induced profound defects in the morphological development of Re + interneurons.

span.label: cells with rudimentary dendrites nonetheless received exuberant aberrant intracortical innervation
span.quote: It is interesting that, despite developing a rudimentary dendritic tree, Dlx5 / 6-Cre;NR1 fl/fl interneurons received exuberant yet aberrant intracortical innervation.

span.label: VAMP2 (vesicle-associated protein 2)
span.quote: Consistent with the expression of the toxin, we found a marked reduction in the levels of vesicle-associated protein 2 (VAMP2), a synaptic protein cleaved by TeLC and required for synaptic vesicular release ( Supplementary Fig. 8 ).

span.label: the single starter cell approach
